results.title: Robometer · reproduction versus paper Table XII
results.text: Our reproduction is 0.007 below the reported OOD mean. This supports a close numerical reproduction, not an identical end-to-end paper run.
results.caption: Paper v2 Table XII, final Robometer column (RBM-1M training). Native progress head; five released-recipe query frames including frame 0; eight causal context frames. Full native compiler parity is verified on our saved predictions. The release selects prefix element j at query j with last_frame_only=False; the adapted comparison below uses each prefix’s final prediction and frame-4 warmup instead. Current-frame VOC on the released grid is 0.879; warmup-grid VOC is 0.832, or 0.840 without endpoints. We sample at most 30 robot rows per dataset before retaining successes (72 total). Exact paper sample IDs, historical code/checkpoint revisions and runtime have not been verified. Our inference adapter uses batch size 1 and SDPA, versus batch size 32 in the released command; bin conversion explicitly uses float32 logits. Therefore metric-code parity does not establish bitwise inference parity.

results.title: Our models versus Robometer · same timestamps
results.text: Robometer’s released-recipe VOC is 0.938 versus 0.945 reported in the paper. In the original T=1 comparison on 72 successful episodes across six datasets, Robometer progress has the highest endpoint-excluded VOC (0.840); the best PSI variant is DT + S5 (0.812). Including the goal-identical endpoint changes the comparison: DT scores 0.896 versus Robometer 0.832.
results.caption: Pearson(score, released-frame index) within each successful episode; average within each dataset, then equally across six datasets. Five common queries; the first is moved from frame 0 to frame 4 so S5 has causal history. Endpoint-excluded uses four queries. Constant/undefined correlations count as zero, matching the release. A clock scores 1 by construction: VOC tests ordering, not task understanding. Exact final goals are hindsight information; excluding the identical endpoint reduces that shortcut but does not remove hindsight.

explanation.title: Why these values differ from the paper-reproduction number
paragraphs: Two things change: which Robometer prediction we select, and when we query the models. Robometer returns predictions for its eight input frames. The released benchmark code selects prefix element j at query j, which is usually an earlier frame. Our comparison selects the current frame’s prediction. We also move the first query from frame 0 to frame 4 so PSI S5 has five causal observations.

For a 64-frame video, the released selection measures predictions associated with frames 0, 2, 9, 20, 36. The shared comparison measures frames 4, 15, 31, 47, 63; the endpoint-excluded version drops frame 63. These example indices depend on video length.

explanation.note: The measured changes come from evaluating different outputs and portions of the trajectory, using the same model weights. Later progress can plateau or fluctuate, and removing the initial low-progress anchor can reduce correlation with time; these are possible explanations for the decrease, not separately established causes. The 0.938 result checks reproduction of the released benchmark. The 0.832/0.840 results compare models at the same current observations. Do not compare the former directly with PSI’s shared-timestamp scores.

results.title: DT temperature sweep · same images and timestamps
results.text: Best endpoint-excluded VOC in this sweep: T=0.3 (0.844); existing T=1 scores 0.799. This is an exploratory comparison on the public evaluation cohort.
results.caption: T=0 uses the highest-probability DT bin (argmax). T>0 uses the expected bin under softmax(DT logits / T), restricted to valid DT bins. All five outputs are deterministic; no random token sampling. Negative distance is used for VOC. Same 72 successful episodes, exact own goals, 235 patches/image and equally weighted six-dataset means. T=1 reproduces the previous DT result. This table changes only DT temperature; the separate T=0.3 follow-up reports other variants. Selecting the best public temperature is not an independently validated improvement.

results.title: T=0.3 follow-up · surprisal and frozen fusions
results.text: At T=0.3, the highest endpoint-excluded PSI VOC is DT: 0.844. Robometer remains 0.840 on these queries.
results.caption: Exploratory follow-up on the same public cohort after selecting T=0.3 in the DT sweep; no independent validation claim. S1/S3/S5 use log_softmax(full-vocabulary logits / 0.3) with unchanged teacher forcing and sequences. DT uses its T=0.3 expected-bin score. Both components change in DT+S fusions; original ABC means, standard deviations and coefficients remain fixed, with no public refit. Same 72 successful episodes, 235 patches/image, goals and query times. The main T=1 table is retained as the original comparison.

results.title: Temperature × cameras · rgb + rgblh
results.text: Best rgb + rgblh setting: T=0.7, endpoint-excluded VOC 0.956. Best rgb-only setting on these same episodes: T=0.5, VOC 0.943. Temperature is selected on this exploratory subset.
results.caption: Endpoint-excluded VOC (Pearson correlation of negative DT with frame index; constant curves count as zero); identical 16 successful paired episodes (6 MIT Franka, 10 UTD SO101), equal mean of the two datasets. This subset is not comparable to the full six-dataset mean above. Sequence: rgb0,rgblh0,rgb0^g,dt0; the same external final goal is used throughout. Current images share the released-frame index, with no observation history. Only rgblh is swept, as requested; this is one wrist camera, not two. 235 patches per image; 3526 input tokens with wrist, 2351 without. T=0 is argmax; other temperatures use expected valid DT bins under softmax(logits/T), with no random sampling. At the selected multiview T=0.7, endpoint-included VOC is 0.962; all per-dataset and included/excluded results are downloadable. T=1 reproduces the earlier camera experiment. MIT pairing is reconstructed from source-loader order; UTD matches episode index and task/outcome. Released frame counts and fps match and paired images were inspected; raw capture timestamps are absent, so subframe synchronization remains unverified. Temperature selection is exploratory, not held-out validation.

results.caption: rgbN denotes a PSI frame slot; ^g denotes the goal role. R = max(1, final released-frame index − current index). DT and DINO use one current observation plus a goal, with no observation history. S3 uses t−2,t−1,t and S5 uses t−4,…,t: one released-frame gap. Robometer samples eight frames uniformly over the observed prefix 0…t, so its gap grows with t (at t=63: 0,9,18,27,36,45,54,63). Evaluation query spacing is separate: for a 64-frame clip the shared queries are 4,15,31,47,63. Released-frame gaps are not known physical seconds. Surprisal scores all four content codes in each of 235 goal patches (940 tokens), excluding pointers; sum within a patch, then average patches, using full-vocabulary probabilities and teacher-forced actual goal codes. This historical RWM definition differs from PSI2 predictor defaults (first code per patch, RGB-local probabilities). Every PSI image uses 235/336 patches (69.94%); S1/S3/S5 use 2349/4699/7049 tokens. S3/S5 exceed the checkpoint’s 4096-token training length.
